entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the State.

2. By means of this application, the Petitioner seeks grant of bail U/s.438 Cr.P.C. in apprehension of arrest for his alleged involvement in the offences U/s. 419/420/469/479/294/506/34, I.P.C. in connection with G.R. Case No.238 of 2023 arising out of Bhadrak P.S. Case No.67 of 2023 pending in the court of the learned S.D.J.M., Bhadrak.

3. As submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner and reveals from the application besides the documents supplemented along with the application that pursuant to the transaction between the informant and the Petitioner with regard to the sale and purchase of the land, there was some financial transactions and allegedly the Petitioner received a sum of Rs.25,50,000/- (Twenty-five lakhs fifty thousand) in his account and in the account of his mother, which the learned counsel for the Petitioner fairly submits and undertakes to // 2 // refund to the Informant.
As regards the other aspects of the dispute, preliminarily it relates to a dispute of civil nature and the litigation has also been brought to the court in civil side.

4. In that view of the matter, having regard to the submission of the learned counsel for the Petitioner, nature of the allegations, the circumstances appearing in the case, the seriousness and gravity of the offences, while this court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail, it is directed that, in the event the Petitioner surrenders and moves for bail before the learned S.D.J.M., Bhadrak in the aforesaid G.R. Case No.238 of 2023 within a period of three weeks from today, he shall be allowed Sonali Sahoo vs State Of Odisha ....

1 to go on bail on such terms and conditions as would be deemed just and proper by the said court,
but subject to the following further conditions - (i) The Petitioner shall appear before the I.O. and shall cooperate with the investigation as and when required by the I.O.
(ii) He shall also appear before the trial court on each date of posting of the case unless specifically exempted from such appearance by the court in seisin over the matter.
(iii) He shall refund a sum of Rs.25,50,000/- (Rupees Twenty-five Lakhs Fifty Thousand) along with accrued interest, as agreed upon by him, in favour of the informant within fifteen days.
(iv) Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail of the Petitioner.
5. The ABLAPL is disposed of accordingly.
( Chittaranjan Dash ) Judge S.K. Parida Sonali Sahoo vs State Of Odisha ....
